body:
Reply with plain text only: no JSON, no code fences, no commentary before or after. Do not send messages to anyone else.

You are drafting lines for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon" (an original story; use only the names and facts given here and invent no new people, places or history). The player leads a party of adventurers; never name, describe, gender or give a face to the player's heroes. The scene is the Ghostlight Express, a ghost train running through a green spirit mist called the Shroud: faded 1920s luxury cars (brass lamps, velvet, mahogany), pale ghost passengers, and six "haints" (lost souls bound to the train by unfinished business). Its conductor is the Vagrant, an amiable frog-man fiddler.

PART A. NARRATOR LINES. The Narrator is the Vagrant telling the tale afterwards. Rules: second person ("you"), present tense, ONE or TWO short sentences (under 200 characters each line), no game words (no "save", "damage", "round", "turn", "check", "roll", "hit points", "prone", "frightened", no numbers), never says what the heroes think or feel, says only what is seen, heard or smelled. Folksy, warm, wry Southern drawl in word choice and rhythm, with a dropped g ("rollin'") in about one line in three. Write exactly the number of variants asked for each key. Format each key on its own line as "~ key", then each variant on its own line starting with "| ".

Fight moments (each plays during a fight against that haint, when its trick happens; 2 variants each):
~ haint:weeping  (the Sweetheart, a weeping young woman ghost clutching a locket, lets her grief wash over one of you; it chills the heart)
~ haint:last_song  (the Songstress, a smoky jazz singer ghost in the lounge car, sings a few bars and the sound holds everyone still to listen)
~ haint:food_fight  (the Daydreamer, a ghost boy in overalls in the dining car, throws a phantom plate or pie at one of you)
~ haint:heaving_deck  (the Mariner, an old sea-dog ghost in the mail car, brings the sea: the floor heaves and rolls like a ship's deck in a gale and knocks folks off their feet)
~ haint:flung_baggage  (the Jailbird, a starving convict ghost with ball and chain in the baggage car, swings his chain and a suitcase comes flying off the stacks at one of you)
~ haint:pratfall  (the Harlequin, an ashamed jester ghost in the circus car, cartwheels close and her painted grin is a terrible thing to see)

Shroud breach (a fight that happens once, after the third haint is freed: a window bursts, the green mist pours in and turns ghost passengers hostile, until the Vagrant blows the train whistle and the glass knits shut):
~ breach:spill  (2 variants: the mist pours through the broken window and another pale passenger in it turns ugly)
~ breach:whistle  (1 variant: the train whistle screams from up front and the broken window knits itself whole)

Keepsakes (1 variant each; a haint, freed, leaves something behind for the party as it fades; describe the object only):
~ haint:keepsake_sweetheart  (a worn lucky rabbit's foot on a ribbon, a gift from her beloved)
~ haint:keepsake_songstress  (a small cut-glass bottle of her perfume)
~ haint:keepsake_daydreamer  (a tin wind-up toy amulet with a little clockwork face)
~ haint:keepsake_mariner  (his old clay pipe, still warm)
~ haint:keepsake_jailbird  (an odd iron key with too many teeth)
~ haint:keepsake_harlequin  (a striped circus sparkler wand)

Places and finds (1 variant each unless asked):
~ enter:g2_porters_beat  (the sleeper car's corridor at night: the lamps are turned low, and a hollow-eyed ghost porter in a faded uniform walks it slow with a lantern, back and forth, watching; a careful step might slip by him)
~ open:g1_carpetbag  (a carpetbag left on the luggage rack of the passenger car; inside a few coins and a small healing draught)
~ open:g2_vanity_case  (a lady's vanity case in a sleeper cabin: powder, combs, a few coins)
~ open:g2_hatbox  (a hatbox under a berth: a crushed hat and a coin purse)
~ search:g2_berth_panel  (a loose mahogany panel behind a berth hides a set of old bone pipes, the kind that play a tune that raises the hair)
~ check:investigation:g2_berth_panel:failure  (you feel the panelling and find only tight joints and dust)
~ open:g3_bar_till  (the lounge bar's brass till, a little coin left in it)
~ open:g3_liquor_cabinet  (a liquor cabinet of dusty bottles)
~ open:g4_waiters_station  (the dining car waiter's station: folded napkins, silver, a tip jar)
~ search:g4_dumbwaiter  (a dumbwaiter hatch in the dining car wall; in its little lift sits a stoppered red healing potion)
~ check:perception:g4_dumbwaiter:failure  (you find only a rattling panel)
~ open:g5_strongbox  (the mail car's registered-mail strongbox, forced or unlocked: sealed envelopes of coin)
~ trap:g5_root_snare:found  (you spot black, root-like tendrils coiled under the spilled letters on the mail car floor, waiting)
~ trap:g5_root_snare:triggered  (2 variants: black roots whip out of the spilled letters and snatch at an ankle, then shrink back)
~ open:g6_valise  (a battered valise in the baggage car: old clothes and a few coins)
~ open:g7_padlocked_cage  (a padlocked circus animal cage, opened; inside on old straw sits a small fuzzy rust-coloured bag that squirms like something's asleep in it)
~ open:g7_prop_crates  (red-and-white circus prop crates: juggling pins, greasepaint)

PART B. COMPANION ASIDES. The party's companions sometimes chime in with one short line (under 160 characters) in a conversation. Each line must make sense on its own, right after the line quoted, and must not need any other companion to be present. Keep each companion's own voice:
- rook_coldwake: undead graveyard watchman, union-minded shield bearer; dry, clipped, flat, practical, few words.
- tobin_hayward: scarecrow druid, sharp-tongued rural diagnostician of curses and rot; folksy, quick, plain-spoken.
- silas_vane: fast-talking skeleton-folk card sharp and monk gambling for his own soul; slick, wry, gambling talk.
- delphine_ravelle: theatrical patchwork-doll warlock who treats horror like a third-rate sideshow she means to headline; showy, cutting.
- lucan_houndstooth: earnest wolf-man monster hunter who narrates danger like a nature documentary; warm, grand, gentle.
- cordelia_skein: poised spider-folk bio-arcanist, treats horrors as delightful clinical study; cool, precise, a little cold.
Write each as "N. speaker_id: line" for these, in order:
1. rook_coldwake, after Phillip Druskenvald (a dapper 1920s lord) says of his wife Adela's tarot reading: "You may as well say yes, you know. She'll only ask again."
2. silas_vane, after Phillip says: "Fair warning, my friends, she considers breathing a sign of boredom."
3. cordelia_skein, after Adela complains her husband won't turn a single card for his wife.
4. tobin_hayward, after Phillip, at the train wreck, says: "Let her have it. We could all do with a little hope."
5. rook_coldwake, after Phillip promises to open his personal cases and give the party a gift as thanks.
6. lucan_houndstooth, after Phillip offers a gray Bag of Tricks (a bag that pulls out a small furry animal friend in a pinch).
7. silas_vane, after Phillip offers a snuff box of Dust of Disappearance, "a gentleman's emergency exit".
8. delphine_ravelle, after Phillip says: "May they bring you good fortune under this strange sky."
9. rook_coldwake, after the Vagrant, at the wreck in the woods, says the crashed train is "just takin' a little breather on her side".
10. tobin_hayward, after the Vagrant admits that a haint caught in a bottle will burn in the firebox just like fuel, and he doesn't love that.
11. cordelia_skein, after the Vagrant says somebody planted the black roots that grip the engine, tied tight enough to choke a boiler.
12. lucan_houndstooth, after the Vagrant says the huge moon is pulling a face he doesn't care to look at twice.
13. silas_vane, after the Vagrant, the train mended, says "She's herself again" and thanks the party.
14. rook_coldwake, after the Vagrant warns them to mind their step down in the village and keep their lanterns lit.
15. delphine_ravelle, after the Vagrant says it was a pleasure riding with folks with grit in their craw.
16. silas_vane, after Phillip catches the party fiddling with his locked trunks and says "These are not the contents of a lost-and-found."
17. cordelia_skein, after Adela says her steamer trunk holds nothing but silk, feathers and forty pounds of sequins.
result:
PART A. NARRATOR LINES

~ haint:weeping
| That poor girl clutches her locket tight, and her heavy sobbin' washes right over you like a winter draft. Frost rims your collar in the pale glow.
| A bitter wail rises from the Sweetheart, carryin' the damp chill of an open grave across the aisle. Your breath fogs white in the sudden cold.

~ haint:last_song
| The Songstress leans into the mic, croonin' a low, smoky melody that hangs thick as velvet in the lounge air. Every shadow in the car goes dead still.
| A slow, mournful jazz note curls from her lips, smellin' faintly of old roses and gin. The whole room hushes right down to listen.

~ haint:food_fight
| That little rascal in overalls winds up and hurls a phantom pie straight across the dinin' car. It bursts in a splatter of cold, glowing meringue.
| A ghostly porcelain plate comes whistlin' past the tables from the boy's hand. It shatters in a shower of pale sparks against your shoulder.

~ haint:heaving_deck
| The old salt bellows a shanty, and the mail car floor heaves up like a schooner in a squall. Brass lamps swing wild as the timber pitches under your boots.
| Salt spray stings the air as the Mariner brings the gale indoors, tiltin' the floorboards steep. Folks go slidin' across the slick mahogany like loose cargo.

~ haint:flung_baggage
| The Jailbird swings his heavy iron chain with a mean rattle, sendin' a leather trunk flyin' off the stack. It hurtles straight at your head with a loud whistle.
| Iron links clank hard against the floorboards, and a heavy suitcase launches out of the pile. It comes tumblin' through the dusty air right toward you.

~ haint:pratfall
| Painted tears glisten under the circus lights as the Harlequin cartwheels right up to your boots. That wide, cracked grin of hers is an awful thing to behold.
| Bells jingle sharp and sour as the jester tumbles close, movin' like a broken marionette. Up close, her smeared greasepaint smile looks mighty grim.

~ breach:spill
| Green mist comes pourin' through the shattered pane, smellin' of swamp water and old copper. A pale passenger caught in the swirl bares his teeth and lunges.
| The Shroud billows in through the broken glass, thick and glowin' like foxfire. In its haze, a quiet ghost goes twisted and mean right before your eyes.

~ breach:whistle
| Up front, the engine whistle lets out a long, brassy holler that shakes the floorboards. Splinters of glass leap back into the frame and knit themselves whole.

~ haint:keepsake_sweetheart
| Where the weeping girl faded away, a worn rabbit's foot tied with a faded silk ribbon rests on the floorboards.

~ haint:keepsake_songstress
| Left behind on the velvet cushion is a dainty cut-glass perfume bottle, still breathin' a faint scent of night-bloomin' jasmine.

~ haint:keepsake_daydreamer
| Sittin' quiet among the dishes is a little tin wind-up amulet with a painted clockwork face that ticks soft and slow.

~ haint:keepsake_mariner
| An old clay pipe rests on the mail sacks where the sailor stood, its bowl still warm and smellin' of sweet Cavendish.

~ haint:keepsake_jailbird
| Clatterin' onto the boards is a heavy iron key, forged with a crooked row of far too many teeth.

~ haint:keepsake_harlequin
| On the sawdust floor lies a striped circus sparkler wand, its tip still fizzin' with tiny harmless stars.

~ enter:g2_porters_beat
| The brass lamps burn low down the narrow corridor while a hollow-eyed porter paces slow with his lantern. Tread light in the shadows and he might never spot you.

~ open:g1_carpetbag
| Tucked inside the worn carpetbag are a handful of tarnished coins and a small glass vial of ruby-red tonic.

~ open:g2_vanity_case
| The leather vanity case smells of lavender powder and holds tortoiseshell combs alongside a scattering of loose coin.

~ open:g2_hatbox
| Pushed back under the berth is a round hatbox holdin' a crushed velvet hat and a plump little coin purse.

~ search:g2_berth_panel
| A loose mahogany board gives way under your fingers, revealin' a hollow space and a set of yellowed bone pipes.

~ check:investigation:g2_berth_panel:failure
| You run your fingers along the dark mahogany panellin', findin' naught but tight carpentry and a coat of gray dust.

~ open:g3_bar_till
| The brass till springs open with a dull chime, showin' a few stray coins nestlin' in the wooden trays.

~ open:g3_liquor_cabinet
| Behind the cabinet doors stand rows of dusty bottles, their amber spirits glintin' dim in the lamp glow.

~ open:g4_waiters_station
| The sideboard holds neatly folded linen napkins, tarnished silverware, and a glass jar with a bit of tip money.

~ search:g4_dumbwaiter
| You slide back the little wooden hatch in the wall, revealin' a stoppered red potion sittin' inside the lift.

~ check:perception:g4_dumbwaiter:failure
| You rap against the wainscoting, and naught answers back save the hollow rattle of a loose wooden panel.

~ open:g5_strongbox
| The heavy iron lid creaks back to show neat bundles of wax-sealed envelopes heavy with coin.

~ trap:g5_root_snare:found
| Peeking out from beneath the spilled mail on the floor are black, thorny roots coiled tight and waitin' for a boot.

~ trap:g5_root_snare:triggered
| Black, jagged roots whip out from under the scattered letters and lash tight around your ankle before slitherin' back.
| With a dry hiss, dark tendrils snap up through the spilled mail, bitin' into your boot before they shrink away.

~ open:g6_valise
| The battered leather valise pops open, spillin' moth-eaten woolens and a few dull coins across the floor.

~ open:g7_padlocked_cage
| The rusted padlock drops away, and on the moldy straw inside sits a fuzzy rust-colored bag that twitches like a sleepin' critter.

~ open:g7_prop_crates
| Pried open, the red-and-white crates smell of old greasepaint and hold a jumble of wooden jugglin' pins.

PART B. COMPANION ASIDES

1. rook_coldwake: Best get it over with. Persistence like that outlasts mortar.
2. silas_vane: Lucky for the lady, I haven't drawn a breath since the house foreclosed on my ribs.
3. cordelia_skein: Fascinating. A domestic stalemate maintained entirely through divination refusal.
4. tobin_hayward: Hope's thin soup in a ditch like this, mister, but I reckon it warms the belly.
5. rook_coldwake: Hazard pay. Put it in writing, if it's all the same to you.
6. lucan_houndstooth: Ah, a pocket burrow! Even in the bleakest wilds, a small furry ally lifts the pack's spirits.
7. silas_vane: Now that's my kind of insurance policy—nothing beats folding a bad hand and vanishing into the smoke.
8. delphine_ravelle: Oh, darling, with this lighting and my stitching, we make our own luck.
9. rook_coldwake: Seen healthier wrecks in the boneyard. That boiler's off the clock.
10. tobin_hayward: Burnin' a trapped soul for steam is sour work, friend. Leaves a mighty bad ash in the flue.
11. cordelia_skein: Intentional botanical strangulation of a locomotive. Whoever cultivated this specimen has exquisite reach.
12. lucan_houndstooth: Look up there—an apex predator in the night sky, baring its pale teeth above the canopy.
13. silas_vane: Sweet music in the pistons, conductor. Looks like our long shot just paid out.
14. rook_coldwake: Standard night watch rules. Keep the wick trimmed, watch the cobbles.
15. delphine_ravelle: Do save us the box seats for the encore, conductor—we always bring the house down.
16. silas_vane: Easy, high roller, just checking the lock's integrity—Purely a public service.
17. cordelia_skein: Silk and forty pounds of sequins. A remarkably inefficient carapace, even for aristocrats.
